page: The Microsoft Azure E32_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. Utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization on the x86_64 architecture, the platform allocates 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with two threads per core. The CPU subsystem integrates a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1 data cache per core, supporting instruction sets such as AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES. Memory capacity totals 256.0 GB, providing an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU allocation. The instance includes no integrated local storage or hardware GPUs, requiring external network storage for persistent file systems.

Benchmark assessments show strong memory subsystem performance alongside moderate compute throughput. The instance recorded a PassMark memory score of 2782.12, placing it in the top 25% of evaluated hardware. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 105.38 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 47.58 GB/sec for large-block writes. Multi-core performance occupies the median tier, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 27104.54, a Geekbench multi-core score of 10522.0, and a stress-ng multi-core result of 29786.22. In contrast, single-core execution speed is modest, with single-core stress-ng at 1410.89 and single-threaded gzip compression at 23.61 GB/sec falling into lower tiers.

The instance delivers high memory density, making it effective for applications where dataset residency in RAM takes precedence over extreme single-threaded execution speed. Because local storage is absent, database architectures must factor in network volume throughput for persistence. The server demonstrated 27.42 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and a static web serving throughput of 20.16 GB/sec. These characteristics align the E32_v4 with large-scale in-memory caching tiers, relational database servers, enterprise in-memory analytics, and memory-intensive ETL batch processing.

Operating on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 256.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It features no bundled local disk storage and no GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote volumes for storage persistence. Benchmark data shows upper-quartile memory subsystem performance, highlighted by a PassMark memory score of 2782.12 and 105.38 GB/sec of uncached read bandwidth. General multi-core processing resides in the median performance bracket, recording 27104.54 on PassMark CPU tests and processing 27.42 million Redis SET operations per second, while single-core metrics fall into lower brackets. The E32_v4 is configured for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory data structures, caching layers, and high-memory relational database environments.
